entry_conditions: Observed entry support includes the initial ordered stack with red above blue at world z 0.060/0.020 m, approximately open 0.040 m per finger, arm qpos [0,-0.3,0,-2.1,0,1.8,0.7854] rad and TCP z 0.442 m. It also includes the expanded blue invocation while red remains grasped over its own pad: red z approximately 0.175-0.281 m, fingers approximately 0.0183 m each, TCP close to red and downward motion visible in qvel and causal pose change. Do not require red already released before entry. Shared transition entry can occur during aligned open descent, closing, lift, red placement, opening or retreat if the observed state is within demonstrated support. Forward receives only two causal 47D states; no selected/previous invocation tag is supplied. The learned graph infers manipulation context from both object/goal relations, finger state and global robot motion, so applicability is limited to the demonstrated red-then-blue task intent.
exit_conditions: A useful late exit has the selected block rising or moving with TCP, fingers near 0.0182-0.0183 m each (total width about 0.0365 m), and a maintained closed-command transport action. Typical selected late heights are red about 0.308-0.318 m and blue about 0.280-0.285 m, in world metres. The grasped TCP is commonly about 0.009 m in negative world x relative to the block center; exact coincidence is not expected. Nonzero arm qvel and early lateral motion are supported, so stopping at a single joint pose is unnecessary. A close TCP-object distance or closed fingers at table height alone does not establish a successful lift. Earlier handoff within shared open-descent/closing/lifting support is possible if the successor can finish acquisition. These are skill handoff cues, not additional task-success predicates.
overlap_role: The policy learns its FULL expanded slices rather than a core pickup interval. For demo10200 it shares [80,180) with carry_place_clear during red open descent, closing, lift and early transport; [235,430) during finishing red descent, opening, retreat and blue approach; and [440,540) during blue open descent, closing, lift and early transport. All other assigned trajectories keep their measured expanded overlaps unchanged. On blue entry it must finish red placement before approaching blue, even though the nominal selected object is blue and red is the previous object. Both object tokens are always present in the encoder, with shared messages, learned attention slots and an ungated mean-node path. Role tags in the conceptual skills may differ across the overlap, but the target raw actions agree. No role-based scripted controller, transition cropping or hard handoff switch is implemented.
successor_readiness: Carry/place should receive the same two causal world-frame states, including qpos/qvel, TCP pose, both object poses and both goals. Positions are metres, arm qpos radians, finger qpos metres, and rotations are wxyz quaternions. The external inference agent should preserve its selected and previous object identities as task context if the successor accepts them; this model neither accepts invocation tags nor outputs a certified held-object label. Distinguish a selected object from a held one using finger width and motion, TCP-object displacement consistency, and object height change. Early shared-band entry may still have fingers fully open; a later entry may have a pinched block already translating toward its pad. In the inter-object transition, red at goal height with closed fingers is not evidence that release and retreat are finished: demo10204 265 still has command -1. At demo10200 280 fingers are almost fully open while TCP is still low; by 330 the open TCP has retreated to about 0.302 m. Such information lets a successor continue the actual transition instead of restarting from a presumed boundary pose.
failure_signatures: Watch for TCP rising while the selected object fails to rise, loss of consistent TCP-object motion despite closed fingers, blue moving during red separation, or red being carried away from its pad as blue becomes the intended next object. A small relational distance, fixed finger width or a single goal-aligned XY observation is not a measured contact or release signal. The model has no contact sensor, explicit success predictor, collision detector, IK feasibility check or validated recovery branch. These signatures should prompt external reassessment, not an assumption that repeated policy execution will recover.
continuation_guidance: Use observed state and motion, not original source indices or a fixed invocation schedule. Continue acquisition through descent, closing and lift when the successor is not ready to finish those phases; continue closed-finger transport during a late transfer. If blue is next but red is still near TCP above its pad and descending, continue the learned red placement, opening and clearance transition before moving to blue. If red is at its goal and fingers open while TCP separates from it, the policy also supports retreat and return toward blue. The encoder uses qvel and both causal poses to distinguish these directions, and object/support height to distinguish tabletop blue from stacked red. Two-state motion is suggestive, not proof of grasp or contact, particularly in stationary dwell states. Transfer to carry/place within the measured common support rather than extending this policy indefinitely beyond its acquisition and early-transport training slices. The supplied task completes when red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal under the full rotated-XY containment and z-tolerance contract; do not add release, clearance, zero-speed or sustained-hold requirements to task success.
limitations: Observed phase and boundary bands are support examples, not hard rejection thresholds or guarantees of learned-policy success. The deployment API lacks the original proposal's selected/previous role tags; three unsupervised attention slots replace them and have no guaranteed semantic identities. Identical physical states with different hidden caller intentions cannot be distinguished. The source stack translations cover only about x=-0.361 to -0.339 m and y=-0.011 to +0.012 m, and cube orientations are nearly fixed. No arbitrary source translation, robot-base rotation, object swap, changed support geometry, failed-grasp recovery or wrong-order execution has been validated. Bottom/top height features are approximate axis-aligned support cues, not exact contact constraints. Global robot configuration is retained, but reachability and collision freedom are learned only from demonstrated support. No independent final rollout performance evidence is available during implementation.
